function: Downlink RB-level precoder prediction from past subband PMI feedback and noisy uplink SRS, with SRS denoising and multi-resolution fusion, against channel aging in TDD massive MIMO (pp. 2-3)
system: 5G NR OFDM TDD, BS with 32 antennas, UE with 2 antennas, ULAs; 3.5 GHz, 30 kHz subcarrier spacing, 96 RBs; no RIS (pp. 3, 10)
method: GRU encoder-decoder (GRUNet), ResNet SRS denoiser and 3D-CNN multi-resolution fusion; supervised end-to-end training, labels from PMI or perfect channel, MSE or correlation loss (pp. 6-10)
data_channel: 3GPP CDL-C channel model [50] (38.901) generated with Sionna; 8192 UEs over 250 ms, 87.5% training, rest validation; test set from a different random seed (pp. 10-11)
test_conditions: Trained at DS 300 ns and window 50; tested at DS 10-1000 ns and other window lengths; also swept UE speed and RBs per SB (pp. 12-13)
baselines: Non-learned: perfect CSI, RB-level PMI at t+1, noisy SRS at t, SB-level PMI at t. Learned: PMI-Transformer and SRS-Transformer; own GRUNet variants (p. 11)
metrics: Spectral efficiency and throughput (64-QAM, LDPC rate 2/3) versus DL SNR, delay spread, UE speed, RBs per SB and window length; parameters, FLOPs, inference time (pp. 11-14)
complexity: Big-O order per SB and per RB (pp. 8-10); Table II per RB: 82.52k-356.16k parameters, 0.5M-8.5M FLOPs, 0.022-0.215 ms inference on RTX 4070 (p. 13)
openness: none; data generated with the public Sionna package [51] (p. 10), no code or data released
q1_support: p. 10: "Delay Line (CDL)-C channel model specified in 3GPP [50]" (38.901 CDL-C, generated with Sionna) for training; p. 11: "Testing results are obtained via Sionna by using a different" random seed.
q2_support: p. 12: "trained with a fixed DS of 300 ns and tested across a range" of DS values (10, 100, 300, 1000 ns); p. 13: "are trained using a fixed window length of 50" and run with other window lengths (Fig. 15).
q3_support: p. 11: "(iii) noisy SRS obtained at" time t and the SB-level PMI are the non-learned baselines; "This network serves as a competitor" to SRS-GRUNet (SRS-Transformer, learned); p. 12: "it is outperformed by SRSGRUNet" in spectral efficiency (Fig. 11).
q4_support: p. 13: "models in terms of number of parameters, floating point" operations (FLOPs) and inference time in Table II; big-O orders per SB and per RB are derived on pp. 8-10.
q5_support: p. 10: "simulations are conducted using the Sionna package [51]" to generate its own data; no code or data release, link or DOI is given, and Sionna is a simulation library, not a dataset.
notes: Area 2 chosen: the learned method acquires the downlink CSI in precoder form (SRS denoising, PMI feedback fusion, prediction against channel aging, p. 2); area 3 is the alternative because the output is a precoder and the metric is spectral efficiency. q2 rests on the DS and window-length tests (pp. 12-13); the speed and RBs-per-SB sweeps do not say whether the networks were retrained. q3 counts the Transformer networks, the authors' own implementation of a standard architecture (p. 11); the GRUNet variants were not counted.
